learning_outcomes.text: The student will build mathematical foundations and more advanced concepts of discrete mathematics necessary for the study of computer science, with an emphasis on the algorithmic approach, applications in computer science and programming.
Students will be trained in mathematical culture and way of thinking and argumentation in mathematics.

syllabus_topics: representations of relations (sets, graphs and matrices)
properties of relations (Illustrated on basic number theory: divisibility, prime numbers, modular arithmetic, etc.)
Advanced enumeration: principles, algorithms and complexity analysis of these algorithms
Set theory - cardinalities of sets, countable and uncountable sets (Illustrated on the basic theory of formal languages and combinatorics on words.) Cantor's diagonalization method

Recurrence relations, homogeneous, inhomogeneous, solutions of recurrence equations of the 1st and 2nd order (in the case of complex roots, review of basic operations and properties, trigonometric form of complex numbers.)
Applications to the complexity analysis of algorithms

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment (graded homework, quizzes, activities in exercises, tests)

assessment_rules: To take the final exam, the student must obtain at least 55% of points from the semester. For the examination, the student must obtain at least 50% of the points from the written part. The assessment is split 50/50 between continuous assessment and the final examination. Approximate scale for grading: A 90%, B 80%, C 70%, D 60%, E 55%.
